newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch unions set to demand 4-5 pct wage increase.
newsitem.headline: Dutch unions set to demand 4-5 pct wage increase.

text.p: The economic upturn in the Netherlands offers scope for a four to five percent increase in workers' pay and conditions next year, the country's largest trade union federation FNV said on Friday.
"We are looking at a demand of four to five percent in upcoming pay-and-conditions talks (for 1998)," FNV spokesman Paulus Plas said.
This compares with a demand of three percent during the 1997 wage-bargaining round.
But Plas said a final decision on the federation's bargaining position was unlikely before December.
"We will first need to consult with member unions and we are still looking at various indicator trends," he said.
The federation bases its wage demands on consumer and producer price trends and trends in labour productivity.

Its pay-and-conditions coordinator Lodewijk de Waal earlier told newspaper Het Financieele Dagblad that higher labour productivity, coupled with higher prices for goods and services justified a rise in the private sector wage bill.
In addition to higher pay, the union demand covers expenditure on training and changes in working conditions.
